images.title: A rectangle and its four sides
images.purpose: Show a rectangle 11 cm long and 4 cm broad with all four sides labelled, so that the opposite sides are seen to be equal and the perimeter is the sum of two lengths and two breadths.
images.composition: The rectangle on the left with its four sides labelled, two lines of working on the right.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. At the top, centred at x 728 and y 62, the heading A rectangle in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px). Left, one rectangle 605 by 220 px (11 units of 55 px by 4 units of 55 px) at x 120 to 725 and y 200 to 420, filled amber #E69F00 with a thick dark #2B2B2B outline (6 px) and no inner lines. The four sides are labelled: above the top side, centred at x 422 and y 170, 11 cm; below the bottom side, centred at x 422 and y 456, 11 cm; left of the left side, centred at x 64 and y 310, 4 cm; right of the right side, centred at x 785 and y 310, 4 cm; all four labels in dark #1F2937 bold (36 px). To the right, at x 900, two lines of text: the line 11 + 4 + 11 + 4 = 30 at y 270 and the line Perimeter 30 cm at y 340 (40 px, dark #1F2937). In all 1 rectangle, 4 side labels and 2 lines of text. No other number and no other text anywhere. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a rectangle whose sides are not 11 by 4, or opposite sides labelled with different numbers
any value other than the listed labels
images.takeaway: The opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, so the perimeter is 2 lengths plus 2 breadths.
images.description: A rectangle 11 cm long and 4 cm broad with every side labelled, and 11 + 4 + 11 + 4 = 30 cm.
images.context: Concept image for Perimeter of a Rectangle. It follows the idea of the rectangle in your maths book (opposite sides equal) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student read the four labels, then add. The slip to watch: adding only the length and the breadth.

image_decisions.why: The four labels show that only two numbers are needed and each is used twice.
